reference_title: EM 1110-1-1905, Geotechnical Design of Shallow Foundations on Soils (USACE, 31 July 2025)

sections.title: Purpose
sections.body: [p. 1] This engineer manual provides guidance on geotechnical design calculations for shallow foundations supporting various types of structures. Performance criteria are also provided. Discussion of construction methods and equipment are generally limited to those aspects that are most important to the design engineers. The manual is not intended to replace the judgment of the design engineer.

sections.title: Distribution statement
sections.body: [p. 1] Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.

sections.title: Records management (recordkeeping) requirements
sections.body: [p. 1] The records management requirement for all record numbers, associated forms, and reports required by this publication are addressed in the Army Records Retention Schedule. Detailed information for all related record numbers is located on the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Records Management Site https://usace.dps.mil/sites/INTRA-CIOG6/SitePages/Records-Management.aspx. If any record numbers, forms, and reports are not current, addressed, and/or published correctly, see DA Pam 25-403 for guidance.

sections.title: Associated publications
sections.body: [p. 1] Guidance for the analysis and design of floodwalls and other hydraulic structures is provided in EM 1110-2-2100, EM 1110-2-2502, and the referenced applicable portions of this manual.

sections.title: Mandatory requirements and deviations
sections.body: [p. 1] Due to USACE’s unique structures and their associated risks, policy standards in this manual may exceed industry requirements. The minimum standards are intended to ensure reasonable uniformity throughout USACE; however, the designer may exceed the minimum standards to enhance resiliency as risk and economics dictate.

sections.title: Mandatory requirements
sections.body: [p. 1] Mandatory requirements. In certain cases, design guidance is mandatory as discussed in ER 1110-2-1150. These mandatory requirements are intended to ensure project safety and function. These cases will be identified as “mandatory,” or the word “must” will be used. The term “should” indicates a strong preference for a given criterion and a USACE recommendation.

sections.title: Exceptions
sections.body: [p. 2] Exceptions. No standard can be considered universally applicable. When a deviation from mandatory requirements is deemed necessary, the designer must follow the policy requirements outlined in ER 1110-2-1150 and ER 1110-345-100.

sections.title: Applicability
sections.body: [p. 2] This manual is applicable to military and civil works structures.

sections.title: Soil foundation material
sections.body: [p. 2] Soil foundation material. Analyses within this manual are applicable to foundations supported on soil. Soil is a mixture of irregularly shaped mineral particles of various sizes containing voids between particles. These voids might contain water if the soil is saturated, water and air if unsaturated, and air if dry. Materials include sands, silts, clays, gravels, and mixtures of these components.

sections.title: Rock foundation material
sections.body: [p. 2] Rock foundation material. This manual is not applicable to shallow foundations on intact, jointed, layered, and fractured rock materials. Design on these materials is discussed in EM 1110-1-2908. Highly fractured rock and rockfill can behave like dense cohesionless sands and gravels, and methods in this manual are applicable. The distinction is generally made when the median particle (or rock block) size exceeds 1/50th of the footing width.

sections.title: Load application
sections.body: [p. 2] Load application. Foundation design methods in this manual assume static loading conditions unless due to earthquake. For seismic design, failure zones are mostly based on an assumed static failure surface (pseudo-static) and various parameters are used to characterize these loads. Guidance for shallow foundations on soils subjected to seismic loads is provided in this manual.

sections.title: Problematic ground conditions and ground improvement
sections.body: [p. 2] Problematic ground conditions and ground improvement. Guidance for shallow foundation design for problematic ground conditions and ground improvement is not fully covered in this manual. Available references are provided.

sections.title: Settlement analysis
sections.body: [p. 2] Settlement analysis. The methods presented in this manual cover the general theory of settlement, immediate (or distortion) settlement, primary consolidation settlement, and secondary settlement (or creep). Stress distributions are included in this manual for embankments as well as shallow foundations. Settlement calculation procedures in this manual are applicable to the settlement of embankments when using appropriate stress distributions.

sections.title: Static and seismic slope stability
sections.body: [p. 2] Static and seismic slope stability. No guidance is provided in this manual for static and seismic slope stability. The designer is referred to EM 1110-2-1902 for static slope stability.

sections.title: Design coordination
sections.body: [p. 2] Design coordination. This manual pertains primarily to the geotechnical design components of shallow foundations. However, due to soil-structure interactions which are present to some degree where any structural element is in contact with the ground, foundation design requires collaboration with the structural engineer and other design disciplines.
